title: London's Gymkhana Brings Michelin-Starred Indian Sauces to Every Whole Foods in America
excerpt: With $8.5 million in fresh funding and a national Whole Foods launch, Gymkhana Fine Foods is betting that the American home cook is ready for premium Indian flavour.
body:
Walk into any Whole Foods Market in the United States today and you will find something that would have been unthinkable a decade ago: a line of premium Indian simmer sauces and marinades developed by the kitchen team of a two-Michelin-starred London restaurant, sitting on the shelf next to the olive oils and the artisanal pasta sauces.

## From Mayfair to Main Street

Gymkhana Fine Foods is the retail arm of Gymkhana, the celebrated Mayfair restaurant that has held a Michelin star continuously since 2014 and was awarded its second in 2024. Co-founded by Gulrez Singh Arora and the Sethi siblings behind JKS Restaurants — a hospitality group with eight Michelin stars and 30 restaurants across the UK, US, and Middle East — the brand launched in the UK in 2023 and has already become the fastest-growing premium Indian brand in British grocery.

Now, backed by an $8.5 million Series A round led by CAVU Consumer Partners (the firm behind Poppi, Vital Proteins, and Beyond Meat), Gymkhana Fine Foods has landed in America. The US lineup includes Butter Masala, Goan Coconut Curry, Korma, Tikka Masala, and Madras simmer sauces, alongside Classic Tandoori BBQ, Green Tikka, and Roasted Garlic & Chili marinades — each priced between $8 and $10.

## Filling a Premium Gap

The timing is strategic. Indian food accounts for more than $5 billion in at-home consumption across the US and UK combined, yet the American retail landscape has historically lacked a premium, restaurant-credentialed offering. The Indian sauce aisle has been dominated by mass-market brands that often bear little resemblance to what you would find at a good Indian restaurant.

"For too long, the at-home Indian category hasn't reflected the depth and quality of the cuisine itself," said Jared Jacobs, Managing Partner at CAVU Consumer Partners. "Gymkhana changes that."

In the UK, where the brand already sits in over 1,000 stores including Waitrose and Sainsbury's, Nielsen data shows Gymkhana Fine Foods driving more growth in the ambient sauce category than Heinz or any other branded competitor over the past six months.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRIs in America, the Gymkhana launch touches a familiar nerve. Indian cooking at home is deeply personal — tied to family recipes, regional identity, and the comforting ritual of a pressure cooker whistling on the stove. A premium sauce brand from a Michelin-starred kitchen is not trying to replace that tradition; it is trying to sit alongside it for the nights when time is short but standards are not.

Arora, who grew up in New Delhi before spending a decade at Mars, Inc., frames it in grander terms: "This isn't just a product launch; it's the beginning of Indian food's premium moment in America."

The US launch also follows the opening of the first Gymkhana restaurant in Las Vegas in 2025, part of JKS Restaurants' broader push into North America.

## What's Next

Gymkhana Fine Foods products are available now at Whole Foods Market locations nationwide and online. With CAVU's backing and the momentum of its UK success, the brand is positioning itself for expansion beyond Whole Foods into other major US retailers. For the growing number of Americans — desi and otherwise — who want Indian flavour at home without compromise, the shelf just got significantly more interesting.

*Sources: NOSH, Morningstar, Food Business News, The Grocer*
author: Diaspora Desk
